sections.overview: This small Asian barbet is currently classified as Psilopogon armillaris; the catalogue name Megalaima armillaris is an older combination.
sections.identification: Its green plumage contrasts with a yellow-orange forehead, blue crown and nape, and a warm orange band across the upper chest.
sections.habitat: On Java and Bali it uses forest and edges, often with fruit trees nearby; it is most frequent above 600 m.
sections.diet: Its food includes fruit, including coffee fruit, as well as insects and spiders.
sections.behavior: It is resident; repeated short trills form a characteristic part of its call.
sections.reproduction: It excavates a nest tunnel in a tree; breeding periods differ between Java and Bali.
sections.ecology: Like the Yellow-eared Barbet, it is a forest bird of Java and Bali; its orange-yellow forehead contrasts with that cousin’s yellow ear-coverts.
sections.conservation: Birds of the World lists it as Least Concern, while its range remains confined to two islands.
